# Data and Code Availability {.unnumbered}

The workflow, the evaluation modules, the Slurm submission scripts, the
committed results and the source of this manuscript are available at
<https://github.com/pablobernabeu/secure_local_HPC_speech_transcription>,
and release `r cff$version`, from which this manuscript is rendered, is
archived at <https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23442766>
[@bernabeuSecureScalableSpeech2026]. The first release, 1.0.0
[@bernabeuSecureScalableSpeech2025], predates the evaluation. Analyses
that use the committed reports can be recomputed from the repository.
Rebuilding the full sweep aggregate and the exploratory scorer
sensitivity also requires the recovered inputs of the English sweep,
deposited separately at <https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23442874>
[@bernabeuRecoveredInputsEnglish2026]. The condition sweep, the
multilingual wave, the diarisation,
filler-preservation, timestamp, masking and anonymisation benchmarks
and the reconstruction audit record in their artefacts the commit they
ran at, and the intervals drawn on the repaired sweep record theirs in
a provenance file beside each table. For the jobs that recorded no
commit, `hpc/runs/` and the commit that added each artefact identify
the run it came from. `r ms_dirty_txt`. The record counted any changed
tracked file, and `r if (ms_dirty_one) "that arm" else "each of these arms"`
ran after an earlier arm had rewritten the committed results, so the
flag does not by itself show that the code differed from the commit.
Corpus audio is streamed through the HuggingFace `datasets` library at
evaluation time and is not bundled in the repository. Some committed
artefacts retain hypothesis text. The deposited inputs contain
condition summaries and text dumps retaining references as well as
hypotheses.
The recognition runs can be repeated on a Slurm-managed cluster that can
allocate a GPU by submitting
`hpc/submit_sweep.sh` once per model, with the settings and the cards
recorded in `hpc/runs/sweep.env`, and then `hpc/aggregate_sweep.sh`,
or locally against a smaller subset by running
`python -m evaluation.sweep`. A bare submission runs a script's
defaults, which for some experiments are not the settings behind the
committed results, so `hpc/README.md` maps each GPU job to the files it
produced and `hpc/runs/` records the settings of each run that its
script's defaults would not reproduce. The accelerator comparison
reported here documents changes in decoded text across hardware.

The confidence intervals can be recomputed without a GPU from the
per-utterance reports committed under `output/evaluation/`. Run from
the repository root, `python -m evaluation.bootstrap_ci --report
output/evaluation/wer_report.csv --bootstrap 10000 --output
output/evaluation/wer_ci.csv` gives the interval on the corpus
estimate, from the raw report of the repaired sweep on test-clean,
which is the same file as `sweep_reports_postfix/wer_report.csv`.
`python -m evaluation.condition_ci --reports
output/evaluation/sweep_reports_postfix --baseline raw --bootstrap
10000 --output output/evaluation/condition_ci_postfix.csv` gives the
paired condition deltas in @tbl-condition-ci, from the per-condition
reports of the repaired sweep, and the same command with `--reports
output/evaluation/sweep_reports` and `--output
output/evaluation/condition_ci.csv` gives the pre-repair intervals
quoted in [the Word Error Rate section](#sec-wer), from the reports the first sweep kept. Each of the
three reproduces the committed table exactly, and since it writes over
the table it names, a check is better written to another path and
compared with the committed one. Each also writes beside its table a
provenance file, named after the table with `_provenance.json` in
place of `.csv`, which records the command's arguments, the digest of
every report it read and the commit it ran at. Both modules record the
replicate count and the seed as columns of the CSV they write, so a
recomputation can be checked against the settings that produced the
committed intervals.

The exploratory reader-cluster intervals are regenerated from the same
reports by `python -m evaluation.speaker_cluster_ci`, using the command
given in `output/evaluation/README.md`. The separate JSON report records
the input paths and digests, replicate count and seed.

The exploratory scorer sensitivity is generated by
`python -m evaluation.scorer_sensitivity` from the recovered condition
summaries and hypothesis dumps, using the command in `manuscript/README.md`.
Its separate CSV and JSON preserve the original scores, identify the
shared samples and record the source digests. Reproduction requires that
input bundle, which has not yet been deposited in a public archive.

The canonical normaliser's gain on AMI over the
utterances both conditions score, `normaliser_gain_ami.csv`, is rebuilt
by `evaluation.condition_ci` with the command below, whose `--output`
goes to a scratch path because the paired interval it also writes is
not reported.

```
python -m evaluation.condition_ci \
  --reports output/evaluation/sweep_reports_postfix_ami \
  --prefix wer_report_ami_whisper-large-v3 \
  --primary-condition raw --bootstrap 10000 \
  --gains-output output/evaluation/normaliser_gain_ami.csv \
  --output /tmp/ami_paired_ci.csv
```

The masking figures are rebuilt the same way by
`python -m evaluation.benchmark_masking`, with `--case-insensitive` and
`--ner` for the other two arms, and the footprint estimate by
`python -m evaluation.footprint` from the committed scheduler ledger.
The ledger itself was built by `python -m evaluation.footprint
--from-sacct` from a read-only `sacct` dump taken on
`r long_date(fp_ledger_prov$captured)`. Its provenance,
`arc_job_ledger_provenance.json`, records the query, the dump's SHA-256
digest and each job of the evaluation the ledger leaves out, with the
reason. The dump is not distributed, because it lists other projects'
jobs on the shared account.

The diarisation figures require the reconstructed meetings to be built
first, which needs no GPU: `sbatch hpc/submit_ami_cache.sh` writes them
to disk, after which `hpc/submit_der_sweep.sh` scores the
hyperparameter grids on the development split and
`hpc/submit_benchmark_der.sh` scores the held-out test split, each
submitted with the settings its record in `hpc/runs/` gives, including
the one that reproduces the utterance-concatenation figures reported
for comparison. `python -m evaluation.audit_reconstruction` re-checks
that the rebuilt audio is aligned with its reference. The timestamp
figures come from `hpc/submit_benchmark_timestamps.sh`, submitted with
the settings and the card recorded in `hpc/runs/timestamps.env`, which
also records a run on other hardware that moved one boundary. The
multilingual figures come from
`hpc/submit_benchmark_wer_multilingual.sh`, whose latest arm was
submitted with the settings in `hpc/runs/fleurs_ml.env`, and
`python -m evaluation.fleurs_multilingual` assembles the summaries of
its arms into the committed one. The anonymisation figures come from
`hpc/submit_anonymisation.sh`, submitted with
`hpc/runs/anonymisation.env`. The determinism figures come from
`hpc/submit_determinism.sh`, submitted with `hpc/runs/determinism.env`
for the H100 and L40S runs and with `hpc/runs/determinism_v100.env` for
the V100 run, and from `hpc/submit_determinism_cpu.sh`, submitted with
`hpc/runs/determinism_cpu.env` for the processor run, and `python -m
evaluation.determinism_cross` compares the runs with one another and
with the condition sweep. The filler-preservation figures
are scored without a GPU by `python -m evaluation.disfluency`, from the
hypotheses the condition sweep wrote for its Large v3 decoding of AMI.
The sweep writes them only when submitted with `DUMP_HYPOTHESES=1`, as
`hpc/runs/sweep.env` sets it, and they are not committed, so
`disfluency_summary.json` records the digest of the file it scored.

```{r appendix-grid-caption, include=FALSE}
layer_n <- table(condition_layer(condition_order))
appendix_grid_cap <- paste0(

  " production stages, the composite pipeline, ",

  "the canonical Whisper normaliser. Corpora are ordered left to right by ",

```

# Appendix B. Atomic Stages of the Post-Processing Pipeline {#sec-appendix-b .unnumbered}

The composite `clean_transcription_text` function decomposes into
eight atomic stages, applied in a fixed order. Each stage is
implemented as a pure function from string to string, exposed at
module scope and registered as a condition of the WER benchmark under
the name given below. Two further helpers precede
them, `remove_emojis_and_unicode_artifacts` first and
`detect_and_fix_repetitions` immediately afterwards. Together the
10 steps constitute the `pipeline_full` composite scored in the
main results.

Five of the eight stages assume English vocabulary and are applied
only to English transcripts. The remainder are orthographically
general and always run. The condition sweep scores each of the 10
steps on its own as well as within the composite, so @tbl-condition-ci
and [Table A1](#apa-appendix-grid) have a row for every one of them, the pronoun
rule included.
Like the sentence capitaliser, that rule changes only case, which the
scorer cannot see, so it scores exactly as the raw output does.

```{r appendix-b-unicode, include=FALSE}
# How many test-clean utterances the Unicode strip changes the score of,
# in the sweep reported here and in the first sweep, which scored the
# earlier strip that deleted every character outside ASCII. Each strip
# report is joined to the raw report of its own sweep by utterance id,
# so that a reordered or shortened report cannot pair different
# utterances (audit finding MS-17).
uni_touched_in <- function(raw, uni) {
  j <- dplyr::inner_join(raw[, c("name", "wer")], uni[, c("name", "wer")],
                         by = "name", suffix = c("_raw", "_uni"))
  stopifnot(nrow(j) == nrow(raw), nrow(j) == nrow(uni))
  c(n = nrow(j), touched = sum(j$wer_raw != j$wer_uni))
}
uni_post <- uni_touched_in(post_raw, post_unicode)
uni_pre  <- uni_touched_in(pre_raw, pre_unicode)
stopifnot(uni_post[["n"]] == uni_pre[["n"]])
# Both reports are Whisper Large v3's, as the sentence says: each has the
# mean of that model's test-clean cell in its own sweep's aggregate. The
# repaired strip moves Whisper Medium's test-clean cell of the grid, so
# the counts hold of this model alone.
uni_is_large_v3 <- function(agg, uni) {
  cell <- one(agg$macro_wer[agg$model_slug == "whisper-large-v3" &
                            agg$suite == "librispeech_clean" &
                            agg$condition == "unicode_strip"],
              "the Large v3 test-clean unicode_strip cell")
  abs(mean(uni$wer) - cell) < 1e-9
}
stopifnot(uni_is_large_v3(sweep_agg, post_unicode),
          uni_is_large_v3(sweep_agg_prefix, pre_unicode))
uni_n           <- uni_post[["n"]]
uni_touched     <- uni_post[["touched"]]
uni_pre_touched <- uni_pre[["touched"]]
# "none of them" where the repaired strip changes no score, so that the
# sentence does not read "zero of them".
uni_touched_txt <- if (uni_touched == 0) "none of them" else
  paste(num_word(uni_touched), "of them")
# The conditions the scoring normaliser cannot see, as the sweep marks
# them, written as the last paragraph of this appendix lists them.
inv_txt <- and_list(ifelse(
  condition_layer(wer_invisible_conds) == "Diagnostic ablation",
  paste0("the diagnostic `", wer_invisible_conds, "`"),
  paste0("`", wer_invisible_conds, "`")))
```

The English sweep was run after the two repairs that
[the Post-Processing Beyond English section](#sec-multilingual) reports, and neither was expected to disturb it. The
language gate cannot, by construction, since it only withholds stages
from non-English input, and English is the default, so every English
transcript passes through the same stages as before. The
Unicode repair concerns characters outside ASCII, and English read
speech carries almost none, so on test-clean, in the transcripts of
Whisper Large v3, the ASCII-only strip that the first sweep scored
changed the score of only `r num_word(uni_pre_touched)` of the
`r big(uni_n)` utterances, and the strip as repaired changes the score
of `r uni_touched_txt`. The
repairs matter for the languages they were made for, where they were
measured.

The two helpers come first. `unicode_strip` removes emoji and the
other symbols, control characters and formatting codes that
occasionally surface in Whisper's output, the zero-width characters
among them except a joiner between two letters, which Persian and the
Indic scripts write. It keeps the letters, combining marks and numbers
of every script, fractions included, together with punctuation,
currency and mathematical signs and the degree sign, and maps
typographic quotation marks to their plain forms. An earlier form
stripped every character outside ASCII and so removed diacritics as
well, and [the Post-Processing Beyond English section](#sec-multilingual) measures what that cost. Immediately
afterwards, `repetition_fix` collapses decoding loops, and it runs only
when the user asks for it. A sentence repeated more than five times in
a row is kept once, a phrase of two to six words is cut to one copy
only when it recurs more than 10 times in a row, and a word repeated
more than five times in a row is kept twice, with a visible `[...]`
left where a phrase loop or a long sentence loop was removed.
Placeholders that have replaced real tokens make it brittle, so it has
to run before any masking step.

Two of the eight atomic stages make the model's uncertainty visible.
`undefined_tag` marks the four spellings of the fragment, `undefined`,
`undefine`, `undefin` and `undefining`, wherever each stands as a whole
word and is not already bracketed, with the visible sentinel
`[undefined]`, so that a human reader notices a truncated word instead
of reading past it. An ordinary word that merely begins with those
letters, such as *undefinable*, is left alone. `filler_bracket` wraps
the unambiguous non-lexical fillers (`um`, `uh`, `er`, `ah`, `hmm`,
`mm`, `mhm`, `uhuh`, `uhhuh`) in square brackets, and brackets the
hyphenated backchannels `uh-huh`, `mm-hmm`, `uh-uh` and `mm-mm` whole.
A filler joined to a word by a hyphen or an apostrophe, as in `o'er`,
is not a filler and is left alone, and the expression is idempotent
under repeated application.

Another pair acts on how the decoder writes particular words.
`contraction_fix` repairs a tokeniser artefact, restoring the
apostrophes that the Whisper tokeniser sometimes drops or splits off,
so that `dont` and `don t` become `don't`. Its table is keyed on
misspellings, under an
invariant that no key may be a word that is already correct English.
Seven were, and [the Word Error Rate section](#sec-wer) takes up the cost that error carried.
[Table A1](#apa-appendix-grid) scores the repaired stage, and [the Word Error Rate section](#sec-wer) quotes what
the unrepaired one cost. Alongside it,
`common_phrase_fix` normalises the capitalisation of a small curated
set of lexical hedges that the decoder writes inconsistently, such as
*kind of* and *I mean*, and so changes only case.

The remaining four stages tidy the surface of the text.
`whitespace_normalise` collapses runs of whitespace and tidies the
spacing around commas and full stops, and `sentence_capitalise`
restores the leading capital, in any script that has one, after
sentence terminators the decoder has produced in lower case. The
standalone English first-person pronoun is
upper-cased by `pronoun_i_fix`, which is kept apart from the sentence
capitaliser because `i` is an ordinary word in other languages, the
Italian masculine plural article among them. Last of the four,
`punct_space_fix` removes the spaces the decoder occasionally emits
before punctuation and puts one after it, except between two digits,
so that decimals, thousands separators and clock times such as `3.5`,
`1,000` and `10:30` stay whole. It protects internal full stops in dotted
abbreviations such as `i.e.` and `U.S.` and in lower-case hostnames ending
in a listed domain, such as `example.com`. It also collapses repeated
marks while keeping an ellipsis, and tidies the spacing inside quotation marks and
parentheses. Order matters
throughout, and a regression test in `tests/test_conditions.py`
asserts that the composite reproduces the chained application of the
atomic stages exactly on a fixture corpus drawn from the production
examples.

The benchmark normaliser used by `evaluation.wer` is separate from the
production cleanup, and the Methods give the sequence of operations it
applies. What bears on the stages catalogued here is that it treats
the hypothesis and the reference alike, except for the small set of
conditions flagged as symmetric in the registry, where both sides are
first transformed by the condition under test. Because it lower-cases
both sides and turns square brackets and punctuation other than the
apostrophe into spaces, `r num_word(length(wer_invisible_conds))` of
the conditions score exactly as the raw output by construction:
`r inv_txt`. The registry flags them, and a null difference for any of
them is no evidence about the stage.

\clearpage

# Appendix C. Per-File Dispersion on LibriSpeech test-clean {#sec-appendix-c .unnumbered}

[Table C1](#apa-appendix-perfile-stats) gives the quantiles of the per-utterance
word error rate distribution plotted in @fig-perfile. They quantify the
spread a corpus mean conceals, and also the sense in which that spread
is an artefact of the unit. The median utterance is scored exactly
right, so the median rate is zero, and the upper quantiles are ratios
over the handful of reference words a short utterance contains. A
90th percentile of two ninths, or a 95th of one third,
records that one or two tokens of a very short utterance were scored
wrong, usually with a quotation mark among them ([the Word Error Rate section](#sec-wer)), and not
that a passage was unusually hard. The dispersion that survives a
change of unit is the one between speakers, given in [the Dispersion Across Speakers section](#sec-speakers).

::: {#apa-appendix-perfile-stats}

\needspace{0.40\textheight}
\apamanualtabletrue

`\noindent`{=latex} **Table C1**

`\noindent`{=latex} *Dispersion of Per-File Word Error Rate on LibriSpeech test-clean*

```{r appendix-perfile-stats}
# "Usually with a quotation mark among them", in the paragraph above:
# re-scored from the sweep's test-clean hypotheses (not committed, as the
# speaker-dispersion chunk describes), 81% of the utterances at or above
# the ninetieth percentile, and 79% of those at or above the
# ninety-fifth, carry an error that setting quotation marks aside
# removes.
qs <- quantile(wer_report$wer, probs = c(0.5, 0.9, 0.95, 0.99),
               na.rm = TRUE)
stats_tab <- tibble(
  Statistic = c("Median per-file WER",
                "90th percentile",
                "95th percentile",
                "99th percentile",
                "Files with WER above 0.5"),
  Value = c(sprintf("%.3f", qs[[1]]),
            sprintf("%.3f", qs[[2]]),
            sprintf("%.3f", qs[[3]]),
            sprintf("%.3f", qs[[4]]),
            format(sum(wer_report$wer > 0.5, na.rm = TRUE),
                   big.mark = ","))
)
kable(stats_tab)
```

\apamanualtablefalse

`\noindent`{=latex} *Note.* WER = word error rate. Values describe the raw output of Whisper
Large v3 with the scorer's treatment of quotation marks retained.

:::

The empirical cumulative distribution in @fig-perfile shows the same
thing in another form, as a step at zero holding most of the corpus
followed by a staircase over small rationals instead of a continuous
tail. The full per-utterance table is written to
`output/evaluation/wer_report.csv` and consumed by downstream
tooling instead of being reproduced in print.

```{r claims-check, include=FALSE}
# The abstract is YAML front matter and cannot hold inline R, so its
# numbers are typed. This chunk re-derives each of them from the
# artefacts and stops the render when the abstract and the artefacts
# disagree, or when the abstract no longer contains the phrase checked,
# so that the list below is kept in step with the abstract (audit
# finding MS-15). It then checks the claims the body makes in words
# rather than through an inline number. A check that fails after an
# artefact is regenerated is doing its job: rewrite the sentence
# concerned, then its entry here.
abstract_src <- knitr::current_input(dir = TRUE)
if (is.null(abstract_src) || !file.exists(abstract_src))
  abstract_src <- "manuscript.qmd"
abstract_txt <- gsub("\\s+", " ",
                     rmarkdown::yaml_front_matter(abstract_src)$abstract)
stopifnot(length(abstract_txt) == 1, nzchar(abstract_txt))
claim <- function(typed, computed = typed, holds = TRUE) {
  if (!grepl(typed, abstract_txt, fixed = TRUE))
    stop("claims-check: the abstract no longer says \"", typed,
         "\"; update the claims-check chunk to match it.", call. = FALSE)
  if (!identical(typed, computed) || !isTRUE(holds))
    stop("claims-check: the abstract says \"", typed, "\" but the ",
         "artefacts give \"", computed, "\" (holds = ", holds, ").",
         call. = FALSE)
}
claim(paste("with all 5 corpora decoded again and scored under",
            "17 conditions"),
      sprintf(paste("with all %s corpora decoded again and scored under",
                    "%s conditions"),
              big(n_sweep_suites), big(n_sweep_conditions)))
claim("first cost 0.40 percentage points",
      sprintf("first cost %s percentage points",
              ppt(cci_pre_row("pipeline_full")$delta)))
claim("95% confidence interval [0.33, 0.48]",
      sprintf("95%% confidence interval [%s, %s]", ppt(cci_pre_row("pipeline_full")$ci_lo),
              ppt(cci_pre_row("pipeline_full")$ci_hi)))
claim("damaging 228 utterances and improving none",
      sprintf("damaging %s utterances and improving %s",
              big(cf_worse), cf_better))
# "Cost nothing" holds on clean English, where the paired deltas are
# zero, and in every cell of the grid, where neither scores above raw;
# the composite gains wherever the repetition repair cuts a loop.
layer_cost_cells <- merge(
  sweep_agg[sweep_agg$condition %in% c("pipeline_full", "contraction_fix"),
            c("suite", "model_slug", "condition", "macro_wer")],
  sweep_agg[sweep_agg$condition == "raw",
            c("suite", "model_slug", "macro_wer")],
  by = c("suite", "model_slug"), suffixes = c("", "_raw"))
claim("the layer and the repaired stage cost nothing",
      holds = cci_row("pipeline_full")$delta == 0 &&
        cci_row("contraction_fix")$delta == 0 &&
        nrow(layer_cost_cells) == 2 * n_sweep_suites * n_sweep_models &&
        all(layer_cost_cells$macro_wer - layer_cost_cells$macro_wer_raw <=
              1e-12))
# "Filler" and not "filled pause": the detector counts the backchannels
# (mm-hmm, uh-huh) as fillers too, and they are half of what the model
# emits on AMI.
claim("preserves every filler the recogniser emits",
      holds = dcond("pipeline_full", "retention") == 1)
# "About a fifth" and not "under a fifth": the point estimate is just
# below a fifth, but an interval clustered on the sixteen meetings
# (computed in the audit, not committed) runs from about 17% to 23%.
claim("about a fifth of those a transcriber recorded",
      holds = abs(dcond("pipeline_full", "reference_recall") - 1 / 5) < 0.025)
claim("on 6 other languages up to 8-fold",
      sprintf("on %s other languages up to %s-fold", big(ml_n),
              big(round(max(ml_field("ratio_before_fix"))))),
      holds = all(ml_field("ratio_before_fix") > 1))
# "Until two further defects were repaired": how many repairs it took
# before no language's ratio exceeded one. The summary's arms are the
# states of the code in the order it numbers them, each scored as
# ratio_<state>, and once the inflation is gone no later state may bring
# it back.
ml_states <- names(ml$benchmark$arms)
ml_states <- sub("^[0-9]+_", "",
                 ml_states[order(as.integer(sub("_.*", "", ml_states)))])
ml_inflated <- vapply(ml_states,
                      \(s) any(ml_field(paste0("ratio_", s)) > 1),
                      logical(1))
ml_repairs <- match(FALSE, ml_inflated) - 1
if (is.na(ml_repairs))
  stop("claims-check: in every state of the code the multilingual ",
       "summary records, the composite inflates some language's error.",
       call. = FALSE)
claim("until 2 further defects were repaired",
      sprintf("until %s further defects were repaired",
              big(ml_repairs)),
      holds = !any(ml_inflated[-seq_len(ml_repairs)]))
# Diarisation alone: the timestamp benchmark scores isolated clips, so it
# reconstructs no corpus, and no tuned configuration of it is reported.
claim("than on hyperparameter tuning",
      holds = der_recon_effect > max(der_tune_gain_dev,
                                     abs(der_tune_gain_test)))
# "Default name masking": the entry reads the default arm, the masker the
# command line and the desktop application build when masking is asked
# for, which redacts no name outside the dictionary and none in any
# casing but title case, whatever casings and categories a regenerated
# benchmark adds. Neither optional arm is covered by it: the
# case-insensitive option redacts lower-case names in the dictionary, and
# the named-entity stage redacts names outside it, which is why the
# abstract says "default". The setup requires the lower-case and held-out
# cells, so neither test can pass on an empty set.
ms_none_but <- function(by, kept) {
  others <- setdiff(names(by), kept)
  length(others) > 0 &&
    all(vapply(others, \(k) isTRUE(by[[k]]$recall == 0), logical(1)))
}
claim("redacts a name only if it is title-cased and already known",
      holds = ms_none_but(ms$by_casing, "title") &&
        ms_none_but(ms$by_in_db, "in_db"))
# "Brings linkage near chance only by destroying the transcript": the one
# setting that brings linkage under twice chance, against every candidate
# and across meetings, is the strongest, the milder ones leaving it over
# three times chance, and that setting leaves over half the words wrong
# once the looped baselines are screened out (near_only_strongest and
# strongest_destroys in load-anon). The abstract no longer says linkage
# stays above chance there: that rests on a point estimate from probes
# clustered on a few speakers, as the anonymisation section says.
claim("brings linkage near chance only by destroying the transcript",
      holds = anon_claims[["near_only_strongest"]] &&
        anon_claims[["strongest_destroys"]])
# "As scored, quotation marks included": the ratio keeps the scorer's
# charge for quotation marks, which the speaker-dispersion chunk
# describes and puts at 12.4 to one as scored and 8.7 with the marks set
# aside. If the scorer stops charging them, re-derive this sentence.
claim(paste("As scored, quotation marks included, error rates differ",
            "12-fold across 40 readers"),
      sprintf(paste("As scored, quotation marks included, error rates",
                    "differ %s-fold across %s readers"),
              big(round(spk_ratio)), big(nrow(spk))))

# Claims the body makes in words.
body_claims <- c(
  # Exploratory rescoring reduces the clean-corpus gain for each model,
  # and, as the Discussion says, Large v3's gain "sharply" (by more than
  # half) on both LibriSpeech splits, while moving its AMI gain little.
  scorer_sensitivity = all(vapply(unique(ss_cells$model_slug), \(model) {
    before <- ss_gain("librispeech_clean", model, "original")
    after <- ss_gain("librispeech_clean", model, "edge_apostrophe")
    (before - after) / abs(before) > 0.25
  }, logical(1))) &&
    all(vapply(c("librispeech_clean", "librispeech_other"), \(suite)
      ss_gain(suite, "whisper-large-v3", "edge_apostrophe") <
        0.5 * ss_gain(suite, "whisper-large-v3", "original"), logical(1))) &&
    abs(ss_gain("ami", "whisper-large-v3", "original") -
          ss_gain("ami", "whisper-large-v3", "edge_apostrophe")) < 0.001,
  # Results: resampling whole readers "widened" the corpus interval, and
  # the pre-repair costs "remained positive" under it.
  reader_cluster = (sc_level$ci_hi - sc_level$ci_lo) > ci_width &&
    sc_level$ci_lo < ci_lo && sc_level$ci_hi > ci_hi &&
    all(sc_paired$ci_lo > 0),
  # Introduction: the repaired layer costs "nothing on any of the five
  # English corpora tested", for every model of the sweep (it helps
  # where its repetition repair does).
  intro_layer_free = all(vapply(
    split(sweep_agg, interaction(sweep_agg$suite, sweep_agg$model_slug,
                                 drop = TRUE)),
    \(g) one(g$macro_wer[g$condition == "pipeline_full"], "composite") <=
      one(g$macro_wer[g$condition == "raw"], "raw") + 1e-12,
    logical(1))),
  # Introduction: "the recogniser supplies only about a fifth of them",
  # of the fillers, backchannels included; the hesitations among them
  # fare worse, which the disfluency-figures chunk records. The
  # point estimate sits just under a fifth, nearer to it than its sampling
  # error, so the text takes no side of it: within 2.5 points.
  intro_fifth = abs(dcond("pipeline_full", "reference_recall") - 1 / 5) <
    0.025,
  # Introduction: the fourth test "finds that the reconstruction matters
  # more than any tuning decision available", the abstract's comparison,
  # checked here as well so that the Introduction does not rest on the
  # abstract's wording.
  intro_reconstruction = der_recon_effect > max(der_tune_gain_dev,
                                                abs(der_tune_gain_test)),
  # Introduction: the voice transformation "brings speaker linkage near
  # chance only at the setting that also destroys the transcript". Near
  # chance is under twice chance; the setting must be the costliest one
  # and leave most of the words wrong. Whether linkage stays above chance
  # there rests on a point estimate, which the anonymisation section
  # qualifies and the Introduction no longer asserts.
  intro_voice = local({
    near <- anon_get("linkage_rate") < 2 * anon_get("chance")
    sum(near) == 1 &&
      which(near) == which.max(anon_get("wer_cost_guarded")) &&
      anon_get("wer_anonymised_guarded")[near] > 0.5
  }),
  # Methods: the timestamp and anonymisation benchmarks "decode in half
  # precision on the GPU, as Whisper Large v3 does in the sweep" (the
  # anonymisation benchmark sets it in code and does not record it).
  ts_precision_as_sweep = identical(ts_precision, wer_precision),
  # Methods: every condition is scored on the same utterances "bar one",
  # the Whisper normaliser, which drops the AMI utterances it empties.
  same_utterances_bar_norm = local({
    raw <- sweep_agg[sweep_agg$condition == "raw",
                     c("suite", "model_slug", "n_utterances")]
    j <- merge(sweep_agg, raw, by = c("suite", "model_slug"),
               suffixes = c("", "_raw"))
    d <- j[j$n_utterances != j$n_utterances_raw, ]
    nrow(d) > 0 && all(d$condition == "whisper_norm" & d$suite == "ami") &&
      dcond("whisper_norm", "n_utterances_dropped") ==
        n_utt("ami") - n_utt("ami", "whisper_norm")
  }),
  # Methods: the jobs run after the lock was taken record their package
  # versions, and "the records committed from the sweep's headline cell,
  # the diarisation, timestamp and anonymisation benchmarks and the audit
  # match the lock package for package", the diarisation records being
  # the four test-split summaries. The sweep's AMI task is the one re-run
  # that dates itself in a committed file; the audit of the reconstructed
  # meetings ran the sweep's code.
  lock_matches = length(c(
    wer_off_lock, anon_off_lock, ts_off_lock,
    off_lock(anon_single$run_metadata$packages),
    unlist(lapply(der_runs, \(s) off_lock(s$run_metadata$packages))),
    off_lock(recon_test$run$packages),
    off_lock(recon_val$run$packages))) == 0 &&
    as.Date(det_cross$meta$runs$v100$date) > lock_taken &&
    all(startsWith(c(recon_test$run$git_commit, recon_val$run$git_commit),
                   sweep_version)),
  # Methods: the preflight did not run at the head "of the first three
  # multilingual passes, which predate it". The passes before the last
  # ran at these commits, of 3 to 22 July 2026, and the preflight module
  # arrived in 34066f2 on 5 August, from which none of them descends.
  ml_early_arms_predate_preflight = identical(
    unname(vapply(head(ml$benchmark$arms, -1), \(a) one(a[["code"]]),
                  character(1))),
    c("9ae40a2", "812552b", "c0f58c5")),
  # Methods: the last multilingual pass ran on NVIDIA cards, the vendor's
  # name printed once before ml_last_cards.
  ml_last_cards_nvidia = local({
    arms <- ml$benchmark$arms
    all(startsWith(unlist(arms[[length(arms)]][["gpus"]]), "NVIDIA "))
  }),
  # Methods: the masking benchmark sets every name drawn "in title case
  # and in lower case, bare and possessive, in each of" its carrier
  # positions, so the cases divide evenly over the positions, the two
  # casings and the two forms.
  masking_crossed = local({
    even <- function(block) {
      n <- vapply(ms[[block]], \(b) one(b[["n"]], block), numeric(1))
      all(n == ms$n / length(n))
    }
    setequal(names(ms$by_casing), c("title", "lower")) &&
      setequal(names(ms$by_morphology), c("bare", "possessive")) &&
      even("by_position") && even("by_casing") && even("by_morphology")
  }),
  # Methods: the condition sweep "decoded Whisper Large v3 on" the card
  # the headline summary names; its AMI task records the same one.
  sweep_large_card = identical(wer_summary$benchmark$decode$gpu,
                               unname(det_cards[["v100"]])),
  # Methods: for the determinism check "no package installed in the
  # environment is newer than the earliest of its runs", the environment
  # records of the sweep's run and of the check's runs made after the
  # lock "name the same versions", and the preflight of its processor run
  # "found all" the lock's pins "matched". The comparison's
  # software_source records the date of the newest dist-info directory in
  # the environment, which must precede every run's date, and what the
  # records and that preflight showed; the runs made after the lock must
  # be the two whose records it names.
  det_env_unchanged = local({
    src    <- one(det_cross$meta$shared$software_source, "software_source")
    newest <- regmatches(src, regexpr("[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}", src))
    after  <- names(det_own)[det_date[names(det_own)] > lock_taken]
    length(newest) == 1 && grepl("dist-info", src, fixed = TRUE) &&
      grepl("preflight lines", src, fixed = TRUE) &&
      as.Date(newest) < min(det_date) &&
      grepl(paste("environment records of the sweep's V100 pass, the CPU",
                  "run and the V100 run of the check"), src, fixed = TRUE) &&
      grepl(paste("all", length(lock_pins),
                  "pins in requirements-lock.txt matched"), src,
            fixed = TRUE) &&
      setequal(after, c("cpu", "v100_seed0"))
  }),
  # Methods: the comparison holds "five runs in four hardware
  # configurations, each a card with the node that holds it or, for the
  # processor run, the node alone", the check having run on its cards and
  # "on a processor": the check's V100 run is "in the node that
  # had held the condition sweep's own decode", on the same model of card,
  # and every other run has a configuration of its own, one per model of
  # card.
  det_configurations = det_node[["v100"]] == det_node[["v100_seed0"]] &&
    identical(det_card_all[["v100"]], det_card_all[["v100_seed0"]]) &&
    det_n_configs == det_n_runs - 1 &&
    det_n_gpu_configs == length(unique(det_cards)) &&
    length(det_proc_run) == 1,
  # Filler preservation: the normaliser "removed" a positive number of
  # utterances (setup ties the count to the two utterance sets), "every
  # one of them" with a filler, of which there must then be at least as
  # many among them as there are utterances.
  disfl_discard = dcond("whisper_norm", "n_utterances_dropped") > 0 &&
    dcond("raw", "reference_fillers") - dshared("raw", "reference_fillers") >=
      dcond("whisper_norm", "n_utterances_dropped"),
  # Discussion: within each of the check's four runs "the decodes agreed
  # on every utterance", and reproducibility "held within each
  # configuration in which it was measured": every second decode the
  # comparison holds, the sweep's partial one among them, agrees with the
  # first decode of its run.
  determinism_agrees = all(det_own_agree) &&
    all(vapply(det_cross$within_run, \(w) w$differing == 0, logical(1))),
  # Discussion: the check's V100 run "reproduced, on all" the utterances,
  # the words of the sweep's decode "on the same node", "at a later
  # commit" and "in a job of its own where the sweep decoded the whole
  # split in one process", and the processor run "gave the same words on
  # all" as well. The process is recorded only in the comparison's list
  # of differences.
  determinism_v100_pair =
    det_cross$text$v100_vs_v100_seed0$identical == det_n &&
    det_node[["v100"]] == det_node[["v100_seed0"]] &&
    det_commit[["v100"]] != det_commit[["v100_seed0"]] &&
    det_date[["v100"]] < det_date[["v100_seed0"]] &&
    any(startsWith(det_cross$meta$differences,
                   paste("the process: the sweep's V100 pass decoded the",
                         "whole split in one process"))) &&
    det_cross$text$cpu_vs_v100$identical == det_n &&
    det_cross$text$cpu_vs_v100_seed0$identical == det_n,
  # Discussion: "the words did change from one hardware configuration to
  # another" (discussion-derived checks on which utterances and by how
  # many edits), and "the check's V100 run shares the L40S run's seed".
  determinism_configurations_differ = det_x$differing > 0 &&
    det_h_l > 0 && det_h_v > 0 &&
    identical(det_cross$meta$runs$l40s$seeds,
              det_cross$meta$runs$v100_seed0$seeds),
  # Limitations: the comparison covers GPU configurations and one
  # processor, "all on the cluster", whose nodes are the htc cluster's.
  determinism_on_cluster = all(startsWith(det_node, "htc-")),
  # Discussion: scored again at the code behind the English sweep, the
  # layer leaves the error rate of every language "exactly where the raw
  # output puts it".
  ml_neutral_after_repairs = disc_ml_neutral,
  # Discussion: the deduplication window "costs a little on test-clean
  # and helps on AMI" (Appendix A, Whisper Large v3), a little being
  # under half a percentage point.
  dedup_sign_by_corpus = local({
    clean <- mw("whisper-large-v3", "librispeech_clean", "dedup_window") -
      mw("whisper-large-v3", "librispeech_clean", "raw")
    clean > 0 && clean < 0.005 &&
      mw("whisper-large-v3", "ami", "dedup_window") <
        mw("whisper-large-v3", "ami", "raw")
  }),
  # Discussion: the size of an effect "moving a long way between
  # languages and between models", taken as the original inflation of
  # @tbl-multilingual differing more than twofold across its languages
  # and the composite's effect on AMI more than tenfold across the models
  # of @tbl-models.
  effect_size_moves = local({
    ami <- vapply(unique(sweep_agg$model_slug), \(m)
      abs(mw(m, "ami", "pipeline_full") - mw(m, "ami", "raw")), numeric(1))
    max(ml_field("ratio_before_fix")) >
      2 * min(ml_field("ratio_before_fix")) &&
      max(ami) > 10 * min(ami)
  }),
  # Discussion: speakers stay linkable above chance at "every setting but
  # the most aggressive", which links least, and that setting works only
  # by "destroying the transcript", taken here as a word error rate above
  # one half.
  anon_linkable_but_strongest = disc_anon$lo > 1 &&
    disc_anon$ratio[[disc_anon$strong]] < disc_anon$lo &&
    disc_anon$wer > 0.5,
  # Methods: the timestamp sample "all fall[s] within one ... meeting";
  # the anonymisation sample spans meetings, and its counts are inline.
  ts_one_meeting = length(ts_ami$meetings) == 1,
  # Methods: on the utterances left unscored "the recogniser never closed
  # its last segment with an end timestamp".
  ts_skip_untimed = all(ts_skipped$reason == "untimed_tail"),
  # Methods: the anonymisation sample is the first usable utterances "of
  # each of its sixteen meetings", every meeting giving the cap, and the
  # split has no other meetings.
  anon_every_meeting = anon_cap_met &&
    length(anon_ami$meetings) == recon_test$summary$n_meetings,
  # Methods: the embeddings come from the WeSpeaker model, typed in code
  # font because inline R cannot be.
  anon_embedder = identical(anon$embedding_model,
                            "pyannote/wespeaker-voxceleb-resnet34-LM"),
  # Methods: the filler figures are scored from the hypotheses "that sweep
  # kept for its Whisper Large v3 decoding" of the AMI test split, the
  # dump the determinism comparison reads for the sweep's AMI task.
  disfl_from_sweep = identical(disfl$source_sha256,
                               det_cross$runs$v100$inputs$dump$sha256) &&
    dcond("raw", "n_utterances") == n_utt("ami"),
  # Methods: the multilingual wave's last state of the code is "the code
  # the condition sweep ran".
  ml_last_arm_is_sweep = identical(
    ml$benchmark$arms[[length(ml$benchmark$arms)]]$code, sweep_version),
  # Methods: the anonymisation sample is "the first `per_meeting_cap`
  # usable ones ... of each of its" meetings, "spoken by" n_speakers
  # people: every meeting of the summary gave the cap, and the summary
  # counts the report's meetings and speakers.
  anon_sample = anon$n_meetings == length(anon_ami$meetings) &&
    anon$n_speakers == length(anon_ami$speakers) &&
    all(unlist(anon$accepted_by_meeting) == anon$per_meeting_cap),
  # Diarisation: concatenation leaves "every component higher".
  concat_higher = der_concat$macro_missed > der_summary$macro_missed &&
    der_concat$macro_fa > der_summary$macro_fa &&
    der_concat$macro_confusion > der_summary$macro_confusion,
  # Discussion: speaker attribution "varies widely across recordings":
  # the per-meeting DER of the test split spans more than threefold.
  der_varies_widely = max(der_report$der) > 3 * min(der_report$der),
  # Appendix B: the sweep scores "each of the 10 steps on its own", and
  # the pronoun rule, like the sentence capitaliser, "scores exactly as
  # the raw output does", as every condition listed there does.
  appendix_b_ten_steps = sum(condition_layer(unique(sweep_agg$condition)) ==
                               "Production atomic") == 10 &&
    all(setdiff(unique(sweep_agg$condition), "raw") %in% cci$condition),
  appendix_b_invisible = wer_invisible_as_raw &&
    all(c("pronoun_i_fix", "sentence_capitalise") %in% wer_invisible_conds),
  # Data and code availability: the filler figures are scored from the
  # hypotheses the sweep wrote for its Large v3 decoding of AMI, and the
  # summary "records the digest of the file it scored".
  disfl_dump_digest =
    isTRUE(grepl("^[0-9a-f]{64}$", disfl$source_sha256)) &&
    isTRUE(grepl("wer_hypotheses_ami_whisper-large-v3", disfl$source,
                 fixed = TRUE)),
  # The PDF's title page: the author line the header block sets must
  # carry the name, affiliation and email of the author entry, which the
  # HTML title block prints from the entry itself.
  pdf_author_block = local({
    fm  <- rmarkdown::yaml_front_matter(abstract_src)
    hdr <- fm$format$pdf$`include-in-header`$text
    au  <- fm$author[[1]]
    who <- c(au$name, au$affiliation, au$email)
    is.character(hdr) && length(hdr) == 1 && length(fm$author) == 1 &&
      length(who) == 3 &&
      all(vapply(who, \(s) grepl(s, hdr, fixed = TRUE), logical(1)))
  }),
  # Appendix C: "a ninetieth percentile of two ninths, or a
  # ninety-fifth of one third".
  quantiles = isTRUE(all.equal(unname(quantile(wer_report$wer, 0.90,
                                               na.rm = TRUE)), 2 / 9)) &&
    isTRUE(all.equal(unname(quantile(wer_report$wer, 0.95,
                                     na.rm = TRUE)), 1 / 3))
)
if (!all(body_claims))
  stop("claims-check: no longer true of the artefacts: ",
       paste(names(body_claims)[!body_claims], collapse = ", "),
       call. = FALSE)
```
